title: Forensic rollout sandbox and auto-revert protocol
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: customers need a safe, reproducible environment to run canary and A/B experiments with stored traces, synthetic shadow traffic, and an opinionated auto-revert policy. Current Console surfaces provide cohort diffs and basic per-route metrics but lack an integrated sandbox that ties trace-level forensic views to a playbook for automated rollback triggers. Goal: ship a Forensic Rollout Sandbox feature in Console that lets operators run controlled shadow replays, compare cohort deltas with trace linking, and define auto-revert policies that can be simulated before being applied to live rollouts.
background: Production incidents have shown teams struggle to reproduce divergence between variants: they see metric deltas but lack linked traces and a way to run deterministic shadow replays. This increases time-to-rollback, leading to higher error budgets and customer incidents. The sandbox will reduce MTTD/MTTR for rollout regressions and provide confidence in auto-revert rules via simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a "Forensic Sandbox" entry on rollout pages that can spin up a shadow replay using captured payloads or synthetic traffic
Cohort diff view surfaces per-route metric deltas, token-level latency distribution, and a linked trace view with sampler IDs
Operators can author auto-revert policies (thresholds on metric deltas, error rates, or trace anomaly score) and run a simulation that shows expected trigger probability
A/B and canary rollouts display predicted rollback likelihood in a preflight check before rollout promotion
Documentation and an internal runbook exist with step-by-step reproduction and rollback verification procedures
engineering_notes: Implement a sandbox namespace that mounts a read-only sample of production traces and prefetched KV cache snapshots
Shadow replay will use tenant-scoped replay queues with rate limits and capacity quotas tied to Dedicated pools
Trace linking requires propagating a sandbox_trace_id header during replay to map responses back to captured spans
Simulation of auto-revert policies will run in a dry-run mode and produce a confidence score using historical variance estimates
Plan to reuse existing cohort comparator infra but extend schema to include per-token latency percentiles and model-decoded divergence metrics
rollout_plan: MVP phases: 1) Backend: replay queue + trace mounting (2 sprints); 2) Console UI: sandbox modal, preflight simulator, and cohort diff export (1 sprint); 3) Auto-revert policy editor with dry-run and audit logging (1 sprint). Start with Hosted + Dedicated compatibility; Private mode requires KMS/audit extension later.
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: Scoping workshop with Eng/Design/PM — agreed MVP boundaries and success metrics
2026-02-22: Backend spike completed — replay queue and sandbox namespace PoC running against synthetic capture
2026-03-02: Design review — wireframes validated, trace linking UI iterated to add sampler-level grouping
2026-03-10: API contract drafted; data retention/privilege model for mounted traces in progress
risks_and_mitigations: Privacy risk: mounted traces may contain PII — mitigation: redaction pipeline and tenant-based access controls
Capacity: replay traffic could spike cost — mitigation: strict rate limits and sampling controls with burst tokens
False positives from auto-revert rules — mitigation: require dry-run confidence > 0.85 and two-signal confirmation (metrics + trace anomaly) before auto-enforcement
qa_plan: Unit tests for replay queue and trace id propagation
Integration tests running shadow replay on a staging Dedicated pool with synthetic regressions
Manual QA checklist for Console flows: spin up sandbox, run preflight simulator, apply and then revoke a policy
docs_and_runbook: Confluence: Forensic Sandbox Operator Runbook - steps to reproduce and rollback
Playbook: How to interpret dry-run confidence and follow-up actions
Customer-facing doc: Guided setup for shadow replays and policy templates
review_feedback: From Design (2026-02-28): emphasize trace sampling controls in the primary flow to avoid noisy diffs
From Security (2026-03-04): require explicit opt-in for mounted traces in Private deployments
From SRE (2026-03-08): require a budget-limited Dedicated queue to prevent cross-tenant impact
